archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-driven)
archetype.definition: A quarterback whose value comes from intermediate and deep throws plus improvised scrambles, while his designed runs and quick game have stopped producing.

report.headline: Hurts wins downfield and on scrambles; the quick game and protection are sinking him.
report.take:
Hurts has spent four straight seasons as a reliably efficient passer who also runs: EPA per play between 0.12 and 0.21 from 2022 through 2025, a positive CPOE every one of those years, and top-six rushing yardage among quarterbacks. Four games into 2026 the passing has fallen to -0.072 EPA per dropback, 30th of 42, with a 6.25 yards-per-attempt mark he has never been close to. The Eagles are 29th in offensive EPA and are passing 5.7 points below what game situations call for, so this is a struggling offense built around a quarterback who is not carrying it.

The depth splits show the problem clearly. When he throws 10 or more yards downfield he is excellent. Thirty-five such attempts produced five touchdowns and one interception, +1.19 EPA on intermediate throws and +0.73 on deep ones, both well above expected completion rates. The other 79 attempts, behind the line or under 10 yards, lost value. Screens sit at -0.92 EPA with one successful play in 16, and short throws at -0.31 with two interceptions. His aggressiveness, the share of throws into tight windows, has fallen to 8.8% from 17.8% last year, and his time to throw has grown to 3.21 seconds. That combination looks like a passer who isn't seeing the quick answers open and is waiting on downfield routes. Under-center snaps (19 plays, -0.42 EPA, 29% completions) are close to unusable.

Two things the season totals hide. First, the schedule split the season in two. Against Washington and Tennessee, defenses now ranked 19th and 21st, he posted positive pass EPA, including a +15.9 CPOE day in Week 2. Against Chicago and the Rams, now 5th and 4th, he combined for about -19 pass EPA, and the 12-of-27, 93-yard Rams game alone accounts for most of the CPOE collapse. Second, the 9.5% sack rate looks like a crisis but is mostly who he has always been. He was pressured on a middling 20.5% of dropbacks, and a 32% pressure-to-sack rate is ordinary for him: 38% in 2022 and 42% in 2024. Extending plays is also what produces his best rushing. Eleven scrambles have gained 97 yards and five first downs at +0.45 EPA each, while designed runs are stuffed half the time at 1.25 yards a carry.

The near term gets worse before it gets better. DeVonta Smith (27 targets, the team lead), Dallas Goedert, Hollywood Brown and right tackle Lane Johnson are all out. Backup tackle Fred Johnson is out too, center Cam Jurgens entered the concussion protocol Monday, and Saquon Barkley is week-to-week with Tank Bigsby on IR. The downfield skill set is intact and should pull him back toward league-average efficiency once the roster heals. For now his touchdown rate (seven scores on 6.25 YPA, five of them in the red zone on 13 attempts) is running ahead of his down-to-down play.

strengths.title: Intermediate and deep accuracy
strengths.body: Throws of 10-19 yards have produced +1.19 EPA per play, a 64% success rate and four touchdowns. Deep balls are completing 13 points above expectation. This matches his career, with high-volume, positive-CPOE seasons from 2022 to 2025. It is the part of his game most likely to last, though the samples (22 and 13 attempts) overstate the size of the edge.

strengths.title: Scrambles pay for the sacks
strengths.body: He leaves the pocket on 8% of dropbacks. Those 11 scrambles have averaged nearly 9 yards, picked up five first downs and added +0.45 EPA apiece. The same habit of holding the ball creates his sack total. Since the scramble value has held across seasons in which he led or nearly led quarterbacks in rushing, it is a trade-off he makes, not a flaw.

strengths.title: Red-zone finishing
strengths.body: He has five touchdowns and one interception on 13 red-zone attempts, completing 14 points above expectation. His long-standing short-yardage and goal-line value supports some of it. Five touchdowns on 13 throws is a pace that will regress, though.

concerns.title: The quick game is broken
concerns.body: Seventy-nine attempts behind the line or under 10 yards are both deep in negative EPA, and screens almost never succeed. Some of that is blocking and receivers after the catch, but completions 8.8 points below expected on screens point partly at him. Paired with a career-low tight-window rate, the offense has no easy completions to stay ahead of the chains. That explains an average of 8.7 yards to go on third down and a 32.5% conversion rate.

concerns.title: Sack rate, a familiar cost
concerns.body: Twelve sacks on 137 dropbacks rank 36th of 42. His 3.21-second time to throw is the longest of his recent seasons. The pressure-to-sack rate is in line with his history, so this is a cost of extending plays more than new pocket trouble. With both tackles named Johnson out and Jurgens in the protocol, though, the pressure rate itself could climb.

concerns.title: Designed runs have stalled
concerns.body: Eight called runs have gained about 10 yards total, half of them stuffed, at -0.24 EPA. His rushing has slid steadily from 784 yards in 2021 to 421 in 2025. The designed-run game now looks like a short-yardage tool rather than a source of yards, so his rushing floor depends on scrambles.

trend.note: Positive pass EPA in Weeks 1-2 against defenses now ranked 19th and 21st gave way to -11 and -8.2 against the 5th- and 4th-ranked units. The bottom fell out against the Rams with a -18.5 CPOE. The slide tracks the quality of opponents as much as his form.

nextGame.headline: A short-proof defense, a thinned secondary, and no Smith or Johnson
nextGame.body:
Jacksonville is built to take away exactly what is already failing for Hurts. It allows -0.41 EPA on short passes, the best mark in the league, and holds quarterbacks to one touchdown a game, second-fewest. The opening is vertical: the Jaguars rank 22nd in deep EPA allowed and 24th in explosive pass rate, and they give up 305 yards a game to the position. That is a defense that concedes yardage and tightens up near the end zone. The secondary is also shorthanded. Cornerback Montaric Brown (67% of snaps) and Christian Braswell are out, and safety Eric Murray (76% of snaps) is questionable after a concussion, as is Caleb Ransaw. That is the best route for his intermediate and deep game to work.

Philadelphia's side is the bigger story. Smith, his most-targeted receiver, is out along with Goedert and Hollywood Brown, which pushes Dontayvion Wicks (+0.85 EPA per target) and rookie-level contributors Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper to the front. Lane Johnson and backup tackle Fred Johnson are both out, and Jurgens is questionable after entering the concussion protocol Monday. That could mean a reshuffled right side and a new center facing a defense with the 11th-best hit rate. Barkley is questionable and Bigsby is on IR, so the run game may offer little to keep the pass rush honest. As a 7-point road underdog, the Eagles will likely have to throw from behind.

keyMatchups.title: Downfield throws vs depleted secondary
keyMatchups.body: His intermediate and deep throws are his only consistently positive area, and Jacksonville is weak deep while missing two corners and possibly a starting safety. If Philadelphia calls first-down shots instead of screens, this is where he can steal efficiency. The risk is protection holding up long enough for those routes to develop.

keyMatchups.title: Quick game into the league's best short defense
keyMatchups.body: He is already losing value on 79 short and screen attempts, and Jacksonville is the stingiest team on short passes. Expect check-downs and screens to go nowhere, which keeps third downs long. Long third downs are where his sacks pile up: five already on 40 third-down plays.

keyMatchups.title: Patchwork line vs Jaguar rush
keyMatchups.body: Both tackles named Johnson are out and Jurgens is in the protocol. Jacksonville hits quarterbacks at the 11th-best rate and ranks 13th in sack rate. Given his long time to throw, more pressure means more sacks but also more scrambles, which have been his most valuable plays.

nextGame.watch: Whether Philadelphia's early-down calls go vertical to Wicks against the backup corners or keep feeding screens into Jacksonville's top-ranked short defense.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect improvement from the Weeks 3-4 level, though not a return to his 2022 or 2024 peak right away. The downfield accuracy, scramble value and red-zone rushing are long-standing traits, and his CPOE should drift back toward the positive range he lived in for four seasons once the Rams game is diluted by more starts. What will regress the other way is his touchdown efficiency. Seven touchdowns on 6.25 YPA, with five red-zone scores on 13 attempts, is too rich, and Jacksonville is a poor place to sustain it.

The sack rate is mostly structural and will stay above average. How high it stays depends on the right tackle and center situation. Volume is capped by a run-leaning offense, 27th in pass rate over expected, though a 24th-ranked defense should force more catch-up passing. Smith and Goedert returning is the biggest lever. Until then, his fantasy floor comes from rushing touchdowns and scrambles rather than passing yards.
swingFactors: Return dates for DeVonta Smith, Goedert and Lane Johnson
Whether the screen/short game can be fixed or replaced with early-down shots
How often the 24th-ranked defense forces him into catch-up passing

bets.reason: Philadelphia is 0-4 against the spread with an offense 29th in EPA, and this week it loses its top receiver, tight end and right tackle. Jacksonville's 7th-ranked offense faces an Eagles defense with the league's worst hit rate and 30th-ranked sack rate, so the Jaguars should be able to sustain drives.

He has taken 3, 3, 2 and 4 sacks with a 3.21-second time to throw. Now he plays without both tackles named Johnson, possibly without Jurgens, and likely from behind against a defense with the 11th-best hit rate.

Jacksonville allows one touchdown a game to quarterbacks, second-fewest in the league. His own rate rests on an unsustainable five red-zone scores from 13 attempts, and his top target and tight end are out.

His rushing value is almost all scrambles, nearly 9 yards apiece on 8% of dropbacks. A weakened line plus a trailing game script should create more of them, even though Jacksonville's run defense ranks 7th and his designed runs have been stuffed half the time.

confidence.note: Four games split by opponent strength, plus a heavy injury report reshaping his receivers and line this week.
